idiom_name: tRPC procedures with inferred client types (AppRouter); schema-first gRPC-Web/OpenAPI alternative
implementation_notes: The classic structure - a hand-written remote interface plus payload types mirrored on both sides and mapped in the facade - collapses in TypeScript: server procedures are typed functions grouped in a router, and the client imports only the router's type, so calls are checked end to end with no code generation, no schema file and no parallel payload declarations, while runtime input validation still happens at the boundary. The facade itself remains a server router module whose procedures are named after use cases and delegate to the domain; it is simply expressed as functions instead of a class, and the transfer objects are structural types rather than declared classes. Choose a schema-first contract (protobuf/gRPC-Web, OpenAPI) when the consumers are not TypeScript or the contract must be language-neutral and versioned independently of the code.
pitfalls: Importing a value from the server drags server code (and its dependencies) into the client bundle; use import type for the router type and keep the boundary type-only.
TypeScript types vanish at runtime, so an inferred contract validates nothing by itself - every procedure needs runtime input validation.
Structural typing hides version skew and Date/Map serialisation is not transparent, so wire-format changes need explicit transformers or wire types.
